floor_history.headline: Recon mapped the whole 18-diff gap to 3 mechanisms and closed 14 of them in pure C: floor 18 -> 4 (split-init address accumulation, a shared named static-pointer carrier, and a pre-loop `last = 3` tha

Floor 4 -> 2 and build_insns 134 -> 133 (== target): H4 CLOSED by deleting the arg1 alias and one hop of the end_off carrier chain TOGETHER; H5 (the Case3 `move a1,zero` placement) killed on every C-l

Floor held at 2/133; the last three C-level structural axes (dispatch shape, loop shape, dependence height) are KILLED with measurements, and a sibling counter-example proves our own toolchain emits t

Permuter modality MEASURED DRY: a validated chassis (tmp/perm_60544, base score 60 == sandbox floor 2) plus 63,820 iterations across a directed no-staging campaign and a full-mutation-space campaign f

frontier.hypothesis: The `move a1,zero` placement is decided inside sched1 by the a1 set-up's own INSN_PRIORITY (or by whether it is in the ready list at that step), and the deciding quantity is visible in a cc1 dump. This is s3's frontier and it is STILL UN-RUN — the permuter session did not touch it.
frontier.mechanism: rank_for_schedule (tools/gcc-2.7.2/sched.c:2399) compares INSN_PRIORITY first, then a 3-way class relative to last_scheduled_insn, then INSN_LUID. Both tiebreaks favour the a1 set-up in our build, so target's build must have won on INSN_PRIORITY outright; s3 measured that raising the ADDRESS CHAIN's height does not achieve that, which points at a1's own priority.
frontier.next_probe: Run cc1 with the build flags plus `-da` on tmp/perm_60544/base.c (a small, fast, validated reduced TU — much cheaper than the full text1b.c TU that s3 would have had to dump) and read the .sched dump for the Case3 block; or set BB2_RANK_DEBUG=1 against tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 (the instrumented binary, NOT build/cc1) and read the RANKDBG line for that comparison directly. Record the actual INSN_PRIORITY of the a1 set-up and of the lui/addiu/sw chain.

frontier.hypothesis: The sibling func_8005D46C, whose block our build DOES emit args-first, differs from the Case3 block in a scheduler quantity that is readable side by side now that a fast reduced-TU chassis exists.
frontier.mechanism: Two blocks with the same callee, same statement shape and the same compiler but opposite scheduling outcomes isolate the deciding quantity without guessing about C spelling.
frontier.next_probe: Build a second reduced-TU chassis for func_8005D46C on the tmp/grind/func_80060544/s4/mkws.sh template (it is now a two-file recipe: base_src.c plus prototype-less callee decls), dump .sched / RANKDBG for its first func_80073728 call block, and diff the priority/class tables against func_80060544's Case3 block. Whatever differs IS the answer and converts directly into the C property to reproduce.

frontier.hypothesis: A permuter campaign seeded from a STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT chassis (not the floor-2 candidate) could still reach 0 by a clean route, even though the floor-2 chassis is now measured dry.
frontier.mechanism: The score is quantised, so the permuter cannot climb toward a match — it can only stumble onto one. Its hit probability therefore depends entirely on how close the STARTING form already is in mutation-distance to a matching form, i.e. on the chassis, not on the iteration count.
frontier.next_probe: Only worth doing AFTER the forensics probe names the deciding scheduler quantity: use that to pick a chassis whose Case3 block already differs in the named quantity, then re-launch on the existing tmp/perm_60544 workspace by swapping base.c. Do NOT simply re-run more iterations on the current chassis — that is measured waste (63,820 samples, zero finds).
